items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains lowest men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To what kind of tested recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being numbered
The ordinal is fifth
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: candradvīpa+vinirgate may refer to a work title or a place of origin
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge
Knowledge arose by another's grace
The object known is the Kaula determination
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the individual soul ultimately dissolve?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
The teacher is asked to explain all this
items.inference: The seeker asks where the soul dissolves and requests a full explanation.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme and unconditioned qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The true reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and utterly pure.
uncertainties: The subject saḥ may refer to the soul or to the supreme reality
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified as haṃsa and as an individual of power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also called an individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: śakti+pudgalaḥ may mean an individual composed of power or a power-bearing individual
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: In what form does the vital air abide within all living beings?
premises: Vital air fills with breath
This air is present in all beings
It is described as situated within them
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides within all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is attained by the soul immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
This departure is the condition stated
The resulting identity is named supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is the traditionally transmitted teaching heard within the ear?
premises: Something is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed
It has come down through tradition
items.inference: A teaching transmitted through tradition is heard abiding in the ear.
uncertainties: The exact referent heard in the ear is not explicitly named
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What transformative power is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: This knowledge is heard
Mere knowledge is emphasized
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even the mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The result of this mere knowledge is completed in the following verse
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The state aimed at is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer literally to an ochre robe or metaphorically to renunciation
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months, wearing the ochre robe and free from bondage,

items.question: What bodily freedom and spiritual companionship result from this sustained practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
Association with yogis is attained
Union or communion is achieved
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What practice concerning the soul has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The teaching concerns practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of inwardly prepared person may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully prepared and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: sarva+bhāva+upapannasya may mean endowed with all states or all attitudes
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is named
This essence originates from the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, born of the yoginīs, must not be given out.
uncertainties: sambhavam may function as an apposition or as a second object in the transmitted syntax
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation from ignorance to purity is claimed for the speaker's body?
premises: The body is now called pure
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The change is marked as occurring today
items.inference: The speaker claims that the body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, though it was once struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming the power of time is now sought?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear
The topic is the deception of time
This teaching is called auspicious
items.inference: The seeker now asks to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ may mean deception, evasion, or overcoming of time
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed by this teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching is presented as a certain means by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you; there is no doubt, as to how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be afflicted at the subtle point of nectar?
premises: A subtle point of nectar is indicated
An essence of juice is involved
Even a wise person may burn
items.inference: Even the wise may experience burning at the subtle nectar point.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are esoteric and ambiguous
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may burn at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique of drawing in breath is prescribed at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: A specific bodily location is named
The breath is to be drawn in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Having fixed attention at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is sustained practice
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is gained by one perfected in this practice?
premises: Poison does not enter the body
The person may be bitten by great serpents
The immunity holds despite the bite
items.inference: Through this practice, poison does not penetrate the body even if bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
